segments.title: 第85章 制服青梅
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 85: Subduing the Childhood Sweetheart

In the bedroom, Xu Youyu threw her school bag onto the chair. While turning on her computer, she unzipped her bag and took out the envelopes from inside.

Compared to Ying Chanxi, Xu Youyu had slightly fewer letters.

After all, most of the second-year club members were already very familiar with Xu Youyu's temper, knowing that writing her a letter would almost certainly get no response.

So, many of the second-year boys had silently written their letters to the first-year girls instead.

Among them, Ying Chanxi had received the most.

So apart from a letter from a young first-year boy, Xu Youyu only received one or two letters from fellow second-year female club members.

A total of eleven letters.

Xu Youyu casually tore one open and glanced at it.

Besides the two letters from the girls, which Xu Youyu considered for a moment before writing two replies, she basically scanned the letters from the other boys and set them aside.

She knew very well that sometimes, you couldn't give too many signals.

Otherwise, there would always be boys who mistook politeness for affection, then complete their own self-conquest and self-brainwashing, turning into wish-fulfillment machines, which was a real headache.

That's why she had always maintained a sense of propriety when dealing with ordinary boys.

Only with someone like Li Luo, who, despite often liking to sneak peeks at her chest, had basically never sent her any ambiguous signals, could Xu Youyu let down her guard and enjoy the simple fun of being friends.

But boys like that were truly few and far between, and Xu Youyu didn't expect to run into them often.

Putting the read letters back into their envelopes, Xu Youyu picked up the one Ying Chanxi had given her.

Sister Youyu:

Writing this letter, I'm reminded again of the delightful surprise of our first meeting during the summer vacation

We must be truly fated to have met by chance in Li Luo's family's newly bought house, and to live under the same roof

Through our time together, I've come to know that you are a cheerful and easygoing girl, and our daily conversations are very pleasant

I hope that in the time to come, we can continue to maintain this harmonious atmosphere, just like we have been

—Ying Chanxi

The letter Ying Chanxi wrote her was rather proper. Xu Youyu propped her chin on her hand as she finished reading, then picked up Li Luo's letter.

The moment she opened it, she raised her eyebrows and let out a humph.

To the Gluttonous Senior:

First, some good news.

With this letter, you can apply for a fifty percent reduction in your cleaning time.

Happy?

No need to thank me. If you really must, doing my laundry for another month wouldn't be out of the question.

There isn't much else to say. Since this is the literature club, I suppose I should share some books.

But I'm not a fan of traditional classics, never liked reading them since I was young, so I can only recommend some webnovels I read occasionally.

The book list is as follows:

《Literary Era》

Oh right, feel free to tell me what you want to eat. As long as you buy the ingredients, you don't have to be stuck with fried noodles every day.

But if you really get fat in the future, don't blame me.

—Li Luo

Xu Youyu: "?"

This damn guy!

Why is he recommending webnovels out of nowhere!

And why is her own book on the list?

Seeing *Literary Era* on the list, Xu Youyu's heart skipped a beat in shock.

But then it occurred to her, Li Luo had, after all, been reborn, so it was understandable that he had read her book.

When they were chatting on QQ before, Li Luo had even praised her, saying she wrote better than he did.

Could it be that he genuinely likes it?

Xu Youyu stroked her chin, contemplating this with a strange expression, which then turned into a flicker of happiness.

The feeling of being acknowledged was quite nice.

She then scanned the letter again. She hadn't expected this Li Luo fellow to actually plan on reducing her cleaning workload.

Hmph, he knows what's good for him.

As for the late-night snack, she wasn't tired of fried noodles yet, so it didn't really matter.

With that thought, Xu Youyu had already picked up a pen and paper. Twirling the ballpoint pen in her hand, she considered how to reply to the two of them.

Meanwhile, in Ying Chanxi's bedroom.

After returning to her room, she took out the letters from Xu Youyu and Li Luo and set them aside, then put the dozen or so remaining letters in another pile.

All together, there were 15 letters.

She took out a pen and paper, then opened one letter.

The content of the letter was simple, nothing more than words of admiration, asking if they could be pen pals, and so on.

Some people had already known of Ying Chanxi before joining the literature club, had heard of her fame, or had caught a stunning glimpse of her at school and had long been deeply captivated.

Ying Chanxi was already accustomed to such things; after all, she had frequently received love letters back in middle school.

For a period before the high school entrance exams, love letters were a constant daily stream. She might return from the restroom to find a new one in her desk drawer.

There was even an oddball who sent her a letter written in blood, which was somewhat disgusting. Later, that person was privately beaten up by Li Luo, and only then did Ying Chanxi's rattled nerves calm down.

Ying Chanxi read the letters while reminiscing about the past.

After reading each one, she would write a reply.

The content was concise, simply thanking them for their kind intentions but stating she had no desire to be pen pals. She basically ended the battle in one or two sentences.

She repeated this process, and even Liu Shaowen's letter was dealt with in the same clean manner.

Once she was done with everything, Ying Chanxi let out a breath of relief and stretched in her chair as if she had finished her homework and could finally relax.

Compared to reading those letters, reading Xu Youyu's and Li Luo's was much more relaxing.

She picked up their envelopes, climbed directly onto her bed, and pulled her panda plushie over.

Then she lay on top of the panda, resting her chin on its head, and began to read their letters.

Xixi:

Hello there

When the landlord changed before, I was worried we might get kicked out haha

I never expected to see you

To be honest, I don't really have many friends at school

Other than my deskmate who I often eat with, I basically have no other close friends

So I'm very happy that the people who moved in were you and Li Luo

Going to and from school together every day like this, eating late-night snacks and chatting at night, this is already my ideal, perfect co-living situation

I hope these interesting days can continue on and on

—Xu Youyu

The senior doesn't have many friends at school either?

Ying Chanxi was slightly surprised.

She had thought that a girl with a cheerful and generous personality like Xu Youyu would be very popular.

Hmm... that's not right either.

Ying Chanxi thought for a moment and roughly understood.

After all, her own situation was similar.

Though it was a bit narcissistic and arrogant to say so, girls who were too outstanding did tend to automatically repel other girls around them.

It was as if there were an invisible magnetic field.

And the boys, more or less, harbored intentions that were obvious at a glance, making it really difficult to be friends with them with a normal mindset.

Over time, you would naturally end up with few friends.

But now, having met Xu Youyu and Yan Zhusheng, Ying Chanxi felt it was quite nice.

At least everyone is very pretty?

Thinking this, Ying Chanxi smiled and kicked her feet up, swinging them back and forth in mid-air, wondering if thinking this way was a bit shameless.

Then, with a sense of anticipation, she opened Li Luo's envelope.

Silly Melon:

Let me guess how many letters you'll get.

Based on my deduction, counting the two from the senior and me, and assessing the number of first and second-year male club members…

Probably around 10 to 15?

How about a bet?

If I guess right, hmm… there doesn't seem to be an interesting stake.

How about you learn to oink like a pig?

If I guess wrong, then just pretend I didn't say anything.

Alright, clowning around is over. Let's talk about something serious.

No matter what, we did manage to get into the same high school.

Trust me, in three years, I'll also get into Qianjiang University, so you don't have to worry too much about that.

With that kind of effort, you're better off taking care of yourself. Don't always throw all your time into studying. You should learn to relax once in a while.

I won't say much else.

After you finish reading this letter, remember to find me to learn how to oink like a pig.

—Li Luo

Silly Melon? Seeing the opening of the letter, Ying Chanxi's nose immediately wrinkled. You're the silly melon, she thought.

And he wants me to oink like a pig, what a beautiful dream he's having.

After reading the more sincere words that followed, Ying Chanxi's expression softened a little, but when she saw the last sentence, she rolled her eyes again.

Then, she flipped over, got out of bed, and pattered out of the bedroom, finding Li Luo in the living room.

"Yo? You really came to learn how to oink?" Li Luo raised an eyebrow. He had just finished putting away the letters on the table and asked with a smile.

"Are you treating letter-writing like a lottery?" Ying Chanxi's brow furrowed in anger. Her fair, delicate foot landed right on his thigh, and she slapped the letter in her hand onto the table. "Rewrite it!"

"Delete the part about the bet, expand on the rest, and it can't be shorter than what I wrote."

"Otherwise, I'll let you learn what a pig's oink sounds like tonight."

Li Luo looked at Ying Chanxi beside him and chuckled twice. "I think it's necessary to remind you that the physical gap between a boy and a girl is quite large."

Just as Xu Youyu was about to start typing, she suddenly heard a commotion from outside.

Curious, she walked out of her bedroom. Looking into the living room, she saw Ying Chanxi being restrained from behind by Li Luo, pinned directly onto the sofa.

Her two small, fair feet were kicking about wildly, completely ineffective.

"What are you two doing?" Xu Youyu didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

"Sister, save me!" Ying Chanxi cried with a crestfallen look, her hands pinned behind her back, completely unable to move. "Li Luo is bullying me!"

"Senior, don't move," Li Luo said loudly. "As long as you stand by and watch, I'll cut another half off your cleaning time."

"Is that a deal?" Xu Youyu raised an eyebrow.

"It's a deal," Li Luo said with a grin, then lowered his head and leaned in close to Ying Chanxi's ear. "Still want to shout?"

"I'm going to tell Auntie Lin," Ying Chanxi pouted, dissatisfied.

"Are you sure?" Li Luo placed his hand on Ying Chanxi's armpit.

"Ah! No, no!" Ying Chanxi wriggled her body, immediately begging for mercy. "Don't tickle me!"

"Then oink like a pig once."

"I don't want to... ahahahaha wait..."

Watching this scene, Xu Youyu slapped a hand to her forehead and sighed. "You two are so childish."

(End of Chapter)
